analyst_view.overall: Early view: PSG arrive top with seven straight league wins, but Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes were injured for their last match and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is out long term; they host Roma in the Champions League four days later, so some rotation is possible. Nice (6th) have won four of their last five league games under Olivier Pantaloni, including 5-2 against Rennes and 2-0 at Angers, but are without Antoine Mendy and Laurent Abergel, with Moise Bombito doubtful.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean a little lower: PSG's attack is thinner without Dembele and Kvaratskhelia, Ferran Torres went into the Troyes game seven matches without a goal, and PSG needed a Zabarnyi goal to edge Troyes 1-0 despite 73% of the ball. Nice have scored 15 in 10 and will look to counter, which points to a 2-1 or 2-0 type game rather than a rout.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. That looks about right: PSG win 5.5 corners a game and Nice 5.7, but Nice will spend long spells without the ball here. PSG had only five corners in their 73%-possession win over Troyes, so a big total is not a given.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. I lean slightly lower: per Statz PSG commit the fewest fouls in the league (6.5 a game) and Nice are 16th (9.9), so neither side plays a stop-start game. Unless the referee appointment changes the picture, two or three bookings feels like the right range.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots. I lean lower: PSG lead the league with 19.3 shots a game, but a makeshift front line and an eye on Roma could trim that, and Nice average only about 12. PSG managed 15 shots against Troyes, well under their average.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target, which is high. I lean lower: PSG average 7.8 on target and Nice 4.0, and Nice usually get fewer looks against top sides. Ten or eleven is more realistic unless PSG field their full first-choice attack.
